title: The Ablation-Strength Dial
takeaway: The three strengths of J-space ablation differ only in how wide a band of layers they cover: light ablates L62–71, medium L54–79, and heavy L42–88, in each case zeroing the residual stream's projection onto the top-10 J-lens directions at every position. Widening the band collapses two-hop reasoning from 98% clean to 6%, while agreement with the unablated model's ordinary next-token predictions only slips from 87% to 65%; a random-direction control over the medium band leaves both essentially untouched, so the damage is specific to J-space content.
walkthrough:
In the published article this figure is not a static image. The page's script builds a small table at view time, under the heading "Ablation strength", with a subtitle recording the sample sizes. The table defines the three strengths of [[j-space-ablation]] used in section 3.5, and attaches two summary measurements to each.

The intervention behind every row is the same. At each token position, at each layer inside a chosen band, the ten most strongly activated [[j-lens-vector]]s are identified, and the [[residual-stream]]'s projection onto each is zeroed; the forward pass then continues. Any token already in the top ten of a clean forward pass is exempt, so the model's intended output is not deleted directly. The three strengths keep this recipe fixed and vary only the band of layers it covers ([[ablation-strengths]]).

Layer numbers follow the paper's percentage convention: depth is reindexed to 0–100, so a layer number reads as a fraction of the way through the model ([[layer-percentage-indexing]]). Light ablation covers L62–71, a thin slice in the middle of the [[workspace-layers]] range, which the paper places at roughly L38–L92. Medium covers L54–79. Heavy covers L42–88, close to the entire range. A fourth, gray row is the control: over the medium band, random directions are projected out instead of J-lens directions. The orange swatches deepen as the band widens.

Two columns report the effect, measured on Sonnet 4.5 ([[claude-model-family]]). "Multihop acc" is accuracy on the 50 two-hop questions of the [[multihop-benchmark]]; the unablated model scores 98% on them. "PT top-1 match" is the [[pretraining-top-1-match]]: over 458,856 positions of pretraining-like text, the fraction at which the ablated model's most likely next token agrees with the unablated model's.

The two columns fall at very different rates. Multihop accuracy drops from 98% clean to 68% under light ablation, then 26% under medium, then 6% under heavy — the near-zero figure the text cites. The top-1 match falls only from 87% to 75% to 65%. The random control leaves both nearly intact, at 98% and 96%. Perturbing the same layers by the same recipe along other directions costs almost nothing; removing J-space content destroys two-hop reasoning while most ordinary text prediction survives. That asymmetry is the section's claim in miniature: the [[j-space]] is required for flexible internal reasoning, not for the bulk of automatic prediction.

terms.definition: The first column: which setting of J-space ablation the row describes. All settings zero the residual stream's projection onto the top-10 most active J-lens vectors at each position; they differ only in the layer band covered.
The weakest setting: the ablation is applied only over layers L62–71, a band about one tenth of the model's depth, in the middle of the workspace range.
The middle setting: the ablation covers layers L54–79, about a quarter of the model's depth. This is also the band at which the random-direction control runs.
The strongest setting: the ablation covers layers L42–88, close to the full workspace range of roughly L38–L92. It drops two-hop reasoning to near zero.

The comparison row: over the same L54–79 band as medium ablation, projections onto random directions are zeroed instead of projections onto the top J-lens directions. It leaves both measurements nearly unchanged, showing the effect is not generic activation damage.
The column giving each setting's layer band. Layers are numbered 0–100 as percentages of depth, following the paper's convention of reporting 25 evenly spaced layers reindexed to that range.

The model's accuracy on the 50 two-hop factual questions of section 3.3, which require silently computing a bridging entity. The unablated model is near ceiling at 98%, so any drop is attributable to the ablation.

Pretraining top-1 match: over a corpus of pretraining-like text, the fraction of positions at which the ablated model's most likely next token agrees with the unablated model's. It measures how much ordinary text prediction the ablation disturbs.
The unablated model, whose 98% multihop accuracy appears in the widget's subtitle as the baseline the ablated rows are compared against.
Shorthand in the subtitle and column header for the corpus of pretraining-like documents over which the top-1 match is computed.
Sample sizes in the subtitle: 50 multihop questions, and 458,856 scored token positions in the pretraining-like corpus.

What is projected out: at each position and layer in the band, the ten J-lens vectors with the strongest activation in the residual stream, excluding any token already in the top ten of a clean forward pass.
The Claude model these measurements are taken on, the paper's default subject model.
The chips beside each row name, serving as the legend: orange deepens from light to heavy as the layer band widens, and the control row is gray.

numbers.meaning: The number of J-lens vectors ablated per position and layer: the k=10 most strongly activated directions have their residual-stream projections zeroed. All three strengths hold this fixed and vary only the layer band.
The light band: about one tenth of the model's depth, a thin slice in the middle of the workspace range. Chosen as the mildest setting; it still cuts multihop accuracy from 98% to 68%.
The medium band, about a quarter of the model's depth, and also the band used by the random-direction control so the two are directly comparable.
The heavy band: nearly the entire workspace range the paper locates at roughly L38–L92, leaving the J-space almost nowhere to hold intermediate content.

Two values coincide here: the clean (unablated) model's multihop accuracy, described as near ceiling, and the random control's multihop accuracy — projecting out random directions over the medium band does not hurt reasoning at all.
Multihop accuracy under light ablation: even a thin mid-workspace band partially impairs two-hop reasoning.
Multihop accuracy under medium ablation: widening the band to a quarter of depth removes most of the reasoning ability.
Multihop accuracy under heavy ablation — the value the text calls near zero. With the whole workspace range covered, the model can barely complete two-hop questions it otherwise answers at 98%.

Pretraining top-1 match under light, medium, and heavy ablation. Even at the heaviest setting, roughly two thirds of ordinary next-token predictions still agree with the unablated model — the ablation is far gentler on automatic text prediction than on multihop reasoning.
The random control's pretraining top-1 match: perturbing the same layers along random directions barely changes ordinary predictions, so the 65–87% figures above reflect J-space content specifically.
The number of two-hop questions in the multihop evaluation, the 50-prompt set introduced with the internal-reasoning experiments of section 3.3.
The number of token positions in the pretraining-like corpus over which the top-1 match is computed, shown in the widget's subtitle.
Context from section 4.1: the layer range where the paper's metrics locate the workspace. The heavy band L42–88 approaches it; the strengths are graded by how much of it they cover.
